 Judgment

This judgment arise out of claim petition filed by the claimants against respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "Act") praying for awarding compensation of Rs.35,00,000/- for the death of Nagaraju S was died in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 05.08.2023 at about 5.00pm.

2. The case of the claimants in nutshell is that:
On 05.08.2023 at about 5.00pm the deceased was occupant in the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AB-3291, the said vehicle was driven by its driver with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering human life, without observing any traffic rules, proceeding near Chandrappa Circle, Chandrappa Circle-Kethohalli Road, Tavarekere Hobli, Bangalore, the driver of the said vehicle lost control over the Lorry and got toppled towards left side of the road.

As a result of the forced impact,
the deceased Siddegowda was thrown out from the vehicle and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body and succumbed to the injuries on spot.
Thereafter body was shifted to Rajarajeswari Medical College and Hospital, Kambipura, Mysore Road, Bengaluru and post mortem was conducted on 06.08.2023, body was handed over to the petitioners.

3. It is the further case of the petitioners that the deceased Siddegowda was aged about 36 years,
hale and healthy, working as a Lorry Cleaner and earning Rs.20,000/- per month and entire amount contributed to the maintenance of his family.

Due to the sudden and unnatural death,
petitioners undergoing great mental shock and mental agony. They are put to great financial difficulties and hardship for his livelihood.

4. In response to the notice, the respondent No.1 appeared and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of notice, the respondent No.2 did not appear hence, placed exparte.

5. The respondent No.1 has filed objections by denying the entire averments made in the petition except admitting the issuance of policy in favour of the Respondent No.2 in respect of the Lorry bearing No.KA-51-AB-3291.
It has denied that the deceased died due to injuries suffered by him in the RTA.
It has further denied the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
Further stated that, at the time of alleged accident, the deceased himself was driving the Lorry bearing No.KA-51-AB-3291 and it was self accident.

Further stated that the Lorry in question was insured as Goods Carrying vehicle, but the deceased was traveling as a passenger in the said vehicle and hence he has become unauthorized passenger in goods vehicle.
Further the offending vehicle driver did not possess a valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.
The Lorry has no permit and FC to ply the vehicle in a public place.
There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

Further denied the age, occupation, income of the deceased and also denied the expenses towards funeral etc., Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners are exorbitant and highly excessive.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against it.
6. Basing on the pleadings of the parties, the following issues are arises for determination.

Issue No.1: Whether the petitioners prove that, they are the legal representatives and dependents of the deceased Sri.Nagaraju S.?
Issue No.2: Whether the petitioners prove that, the deceased Sri.Nagaraju S., had died due to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident that occurred on 05.08.2023 at about 05.00 p.m, near Chandrappa Circle, Chandrappa Circle- Kothohalli Road, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru, due to due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AB-3291 as alleged?
Issue No.3: Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as claimed?

If so, what amount and from whom?
Issue No.4: What order or Award?

7. In order to substantiate the claim petition contention, the petitioner No.2 has examined herself as PW-1 and got marked total Fifteen documents as Exs.P1 to P.15 and closed their side evidence.
Inorder to prove its defence the respondent No.1 got examined its Legal Manager as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1.
It has also got examined Investigator as RW.2 and got marked Exs.R.2 to R.4 and closed their side.

9. On perusal of oral and documentary evidence let in before this tribunal, my answers to the above Issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the affirmative Issue No.2 : In the affirmative.
Issue No.3 : Partly in affirmative Issue No.4 : As per final order, for the foregoing;
REASONS 10. Issue Nos.1 and 2: As these issues are inter- linked each other, as such I considered these issues taken together for common discussion and also to avoid repetition of facts of the case.

As I referred above, In order to substantiate the claim petition contention, the petitioner No.2 has examined herself as PW-1 and got marked total Fifteen documents as Ex.P1 to 15 and closed their side evidence.
The respondent No.2 has got examined its official as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 and also got examined Investigator as RW.2 and got marked Exs.R.2 to 4.
The details of the exhibits are given in the annexure of the judgment.
11. The PW.1 has reiterated the petition averments in the chief examination.
The PW.1 has been subjected to cross examination.
In the cross examination of PW.1, nothing worthwhile is elicited.
She further denied other suggestions made by the learned counsel for the parties.

12. To prove the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased, they have produced notarized copy of Aadhar Cards of the petitioners and the deceased, Death Certificate, TC of the decaesed,
Voter's ID Card of the deceased, Geneological Tree and death certificate of fatehr of the deceased at Exs.P.9 to 12 and 14 and 15.
Ex.P.6 Inquest mahazar also shows the names and relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
13. It is main defense of the insurer that the petition is filed by suppressing the real facts in respect to vocation of the deceased.
As per the evidence of RW.2, the deceased was working as driver and not a cleaner.
But the material on record are clearly depicts that there is no reference that the deceased was driving the Lorry.
During the cross examination of RW.2, she has admitted that she has not produced visible/authenticated Video or Photos to prove that the deceased was working as a Driver in the offending Lorry.
Further, she has not challenged the Charge sheet.

Further admitted that, on the basis of owner statement and deceased brother's statement, she is submitting her witness but there is no document proof to show that the deceased was working as a Driver under Respondent No.2.
In the absence of the cogent evidence, it is not safe to belief the version of the insurer.
14. The petitioners have totally relied on the police documents to establish the negligence on the part of the deceased and offending vehicle's driver.
It is no doubt the police have submitted the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle after thorough investigation.
The insurer have not seriously disputing the nature of accident.

Apart from that, the sketch appended to spot mahazar indicates that the deceased was proceeding in a Lorry bearing No.KA- 51-AB-3291 as a Muddiramma vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23663018/

sentences.text: The Lorry driven by driver with high speed and took turn towards right and lorry toppled near Chandrappa Circle, Doddaladamara Road due to which Nagaraju S. (deceased) died on the spot.
The Sketch further depicts that the Lorry proceeding towards Doddaladamara Road and the accident spot is on the left side of the road and it was 40 feet Road.
The sketch clearly depicts that the offending vehicle was moving towards Doddaladamara Road.
The oral evidence of the petitioners have coupled with documentary evidence.

15. A perusal of the charge sheet, the police have submitted the charge sheet against the accused or driver of the offending vehicle which is belongs to respondent No.2 and further the police have charge sheeted against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offense punishable under section 279 and 304(A) of IPC.

The police have referred section 279, 304(A) of IPC against the accused, so,
as per the police documents, the driver of the offending vehicle had a valid driving license at the time of alleged accident.
Hence, it is not safe to hold that the offending vehicle's driver does not possess the valid driving license at the time of the alleged accident.
The Court cannot adopt strict liability as conducted in a criminal case to prove rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the respondent vehicle.
But there should be prima-facie materials regarding rash and negligence to fix the owner and insurance company for payment of compensation.
Therefore, a straight jacket formula cannot be adopted in accepting the rash and negligence on the part of driver of the insured.
The materials on records are clearly indicates that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the respondent No.2's vehicle

So, I hold issue Nos.1 & 2 in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.3: The Petitioner Nos.1 & 2 being the mother and sister of the deceased.
It is the contention of the petitioners that the deceased was doing Lorry Cleaner work and earning of Rs.20,000/- Per month.
The petitioner No.2 has reiterated the same in the chief examination affidavit.
But the petitioners have not placed any material worth in this regard.
As per the claim petition the age of the deceased was 36 years.
The Aadhar Card of the deceased at Ex.P.9 discloses that the date of birth of the deceased is 15.05.1996, as such, the age was 27 years.
But as per Ex.P.11 Transfer Certificate of the deceased, his date of birth is 15.05.1986 as such his age was 37 years.
TC/School document is first document which was entered/prepared before the Aadhar Card.
Therefore, the age of the deceased will be considered as 37 years as on the date of his death.
As I mentioned above, the petitioners have not placed any material worth to show the exact income of the deceased.

So, considering the nature of work, the chart prepared, furnished by the Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru is taken in to consideration, the notional income of Rs.16,000/- pm is calculated to award loss of earning, it would meets the ends of justice.

Therefore, Petitioner Nos.1 is considered as dependent of the deceased.

Then the total income of the deceased would come Rs.11,200/- (Rs.22,400/- - Rs.11,200/- = Rs.11,200/-).
The loss of dependency is calculated as below.
Rs.11,200/- (monthly income) x 12 x 15 (multiplier) =Rs.20,16,000/-.
This is just and proper compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
LOSS OF ESTATE 17.
As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Pranay Sethi case in case of death in the maximum the Court can award Rs.18,000/- in lump sum under the head of loss of estate.
FUNERAL EXPENSES 18.
In view of the Pranay Sethi's case this tribunal has no option but to award Rs.18,000/- under this head.
Except these heads the claimants are not entitled for any compensation.
LOSS OF CONSORTIUM 19.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed in a judgment reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 has held in aragraph No.21 that "A Constitution Bench of this Court in Pranay Sethi (Supra) dealt with the various heads under which the compensation is to be awarded in a death 1 Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram case.

sentences.text: One of these heads is Loss of Consortium.

In legal parlance Consortium is a compendious term which encompasses Spousal Consortium;
Parental consortium and filial consortium.

The right to consortium would include the company,
care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.
With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse."

21 1 "Spousal Consortium is generally defined as rights pertaining to the relationship of a husband wife which allows compensation to the surviving spouse for loss of Company, Society, co operation,
affection and aid of the other in every conjugal relation"
21 2
"Parental Consortium is granted to the child upon the premature death of a parent, for loss of parental aid, protection, affection, society, discipline, guidance and training."13,50,180
21 3 " Filial Consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of the Child.
An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock, agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose their child during their lifetime.
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their role in the family unit."

sentences.text: Consortium is a special prism reflecting changing norms about the status and worth of actual relationships.
Modern jurisdictions world over have recognized that the value of a Child's consortium far exceeds the economic value of the compensation awarded in the case of the death of a child.
Most jurisdictions therefore, permit parents to be awarded compensation under loss of consortium on the death of a child.

The amount awarded to the parents is a compensation for loss of the love, affection, care and companionship of the deceased child".
20.
The Petitioner No.1 being the Mother is entitled for '"Filial Consortium'.
Hence a sum of Rs.44,000/- is awarded under this head.
21. Therefore, the claimants are entitled for compensation under the following heads.

04. Loss of Consortium Rs.44,000=00  TOTAL Rs.20,96,000-00 22.
The next question is the liability to pay the said compensation.
As I referred above the accident was occurred due rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
Hence respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The respondent No.1 has to indemnify the respondent No.2 and liable to pay compensation to the petitioner No.1.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 partly in Affirmative.
23. Issue No.4:- In view of my findings to the above issues, the claimants are entitled for the compensation at the at rate of 6% P.A. from the respondent No.1.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by claimants under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is allowed in part.
The petitioner No.1 is entitled for compensation tune of Rs.20,96,000/- (Rupees Twenty Lakhs Ninety Six Thousands Only) together interest @ 6%PA from the date of petition till realization.

The respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to the claimants and directed to deposit the same within 60 days from the date of this judgment, after deducting any amount paid as the interim compensation.
